feed.title: Fort Worth Makes Rare Earths Great Again at MP Materials' Alliance Facility
feed.summary: MP Materials is establishing a critical rare-earth magnet supply chain in Fort Worth, Texas, at its Independence facility, turning domestically mined rare earths into high-performance permanent magnets. This initiative, supported by General Motors and the city of Fort Worth, aims to reduce U.S. dependence on foreign supply chains for strategic minerals, with a larger mega-complex planned in Northlake. The company expects to produce over a million magnets daily at Independence, significantly bolstering American national security and advanced manufacturing.

feed.title: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) Cuts Fitness+ Audio Staff As Company Eyes Major Service Overhaul
feed.summary: Apple Inc. has laid off employees from its Fitness+ audio division, specifically targeting staff involved in "Time to Walk" and "Time to Run" sessions, as it reconsiders the subscription service's future. The company plans to reduce the frequency of new audio releases and is looking at integrating Fitness+ more deeply into a redesigned Health app. This move comes amidst competitive pressure and coincides with the launch of the new iPhone Duo, with Apple's stock seeing varied short-term sentiment but remaining up 23.3% year to date.

feed.title: Meta’s Muse is outpacing ChatGPT’s early mobile launch

This early success suggests Muse could become another major hit for Meta, potentially leveraging the company's powerful cross-promotion strategies seen with apps like Threads.

feed.title: CCIA Joins Supreme Court Amicus Brief in Apple v. Epic
feed.summary: The Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA) has filed an amicus brief supporting Apple Inc. in the Supreme Court case Apple v. Epic. The brief argues against a lower court's ruling that found Apple in contempt for violating the "spirit" of an order, even without explicit prohibition, stating that such a standard creates uncertainty and contradicts federal law. CCIA President & CEO Matt Schruers emphasized the importance of clear, text-based court orders, especially concerning protected speech and editorial curation.

feed.title: Apple (AAPL) Faces a $2.7 Billion UK Lawsuit over its App Tracking Rules
feed.summary: Apple Inc. is facing a £2 billion ($2.7 billion) lawsuit in the UK over its App Tracking Transparency feature, which app developers allege unfairly favors Apple's own advertising services. This legal challenge is part of a broader pattern of European regulatory scrutiny on Apple's tracking practices, with similar actions in France, Italy, and Germany. Despite Apple's strong financial position to absorb potential legal costs, the lawsuit could force the company to make significant changes to its platform and advertising policies, potentially setting a precedent for its control over the app ecosystem.

feed.title: Nvidia Is an ‘Awesome Company,’ but Its Stock Is Priced as ‘Greatest Company Ever,’ Damodaran Says
feed.summary: NYU Stern finance professor Aswath Damodaran views Nvidia as an "awesome company" but believes its stock valuation, exceeding $5 trillion, is priced as the "greatest company ever." He suggests that the current AI sector revenue and investment would require annual revenues of $8 trillion to $10 trillion to justify the infrastructure buildout, far beyond today's $250 billion. Damodaran posits that such growth is only achievable if AI replaces workers rather than merely augmenting productivity, which would then pose new economic challenges regarding consumer spending.
